newsitem.title: USA: Michigan Muni Bond Authority notes SP1-plus by S&P.
newsitem.headline: Michigan Muni Bond Authority notes SP1-plus by S&P.

text.p: NEW YORK, Sept 9 - Standard & Poor's on Monday said it assigned its SP-1-plus rating to Michigan Municipal Bond Authority's revenue notes series 1996D due Sept. 16, 1997.

--The Michigan State Treasurer's obligation to intercept and, if needed, advance withhold the 10 participating school district's fiscal 1996-1997 appropriated state education aid to pay each district's share of debt service on the revenue notes in the event of a monthly payment deficiency;

--Strong structural features, including early segregation of pledged revenues in the districts' note repayment accounts, which ensures the accounts are fully funded more than one month prior to the authority's revenue note maturity; and
--Strong debt service coverage by the school districts' pledged state aid. Coverage on a total basis ranged from 5.4 times (x)-40x. Coverage of monthly set asides ranges from 3.6x-26.7x.

Revenue note proceeds will fund the authority's purchase of municipal obligations (notes) issued by the 10 participating school districts for seasonal cash flow needs. The authority's revenue notes will be repaid from funds on deposit in the school disticts' note repayment accounts.

Each school district will be required to segregate a portion of its monthly state aid to be received beginning in November in a separate note repayment account to be held by a third party trustee. The district's note repayment accounts are projected to all be fully funded by May 31, 1997, more than one month prior to the maturity of the authority's notes.

If a district fails to make the required monthly installment payment by the last day of any month from November, 1996 through May, 1997, the intercept mechanism is invoked. The borrowing criteria dictates that for all borrowers, interceptable aid to be received after the last scheduled set aside is at least equal to the required monthly set aside, thus ensuring that sufficient interceptable aid exists in the case of a set aside shortfall, S&P said.
